title: The OSI and TCP/IP Models knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the main idea of The OSI and TCP/IP Models?
options: Layered network models help locate where a fault or control applies. The OSI model is a teaching model; the real Internet protocol suite does not map perfectly to seven independent boxes.
A single successful test proves that a system is completely secure in every environment.
The fastest workflow is always to skip evidence collection and make changes directly in production.
Security responsibilities disappear when a technical tool has been installed.
questions.answer_key: Layered network models help locate where a fault or control applies. The OSI model is a teaching model; the real Internet protocol suite does not map perfectly to seven independent boxes.
questions.explanation: The lesson's core idea is: Layered network models help locate where a fault or control applies. The OSI model is a teaching model; the real Internet protocol suite does not map perfectly to seven independent boxes. The other options overstate what one test or tool can prove and ignore the need for context, evidence, and governance.

questions.prompt: You are applying The OSI and TCP/IP Models to a new scenario. What is the best first step?
options: Define scope and expected behavior, collect relevant evidence, and verify the result in an authorized or synthetic environment.
Repeat the same test against unrelated public systems to collect more data.
Disable useful logging so the test output looks simpler.
Assume an unfamiliar result proves malicious intent without corroboration.
questions.answer_key: Define scope and expected behavior, collect relevant evidence, and verify the result in an authorized or synthetic environment.
questions.explanation: Bound the work, define expected behavior, and collect relevant evidence in a safe and authorized context before drawing conclusions.

questions.prompt: Which practice most improves the reliability of work on The OSI and TCP/IP Models?
options: Document assumptions and limitations, then select a proportionate defensive next step based on evidence and current guidance.
Publish raw secrets and personal information so someone else can reproduce the test.
Treat a teaching example as proof of production security without retesting.
Skip documenting exceptions because they make the report more complicated.
questions.answer_key: Document assumptions and limitations, then select a proportionate defensive next step based on evidence and current guidance.
questions.explanation: Security claims should be backed by reproducible evidence and clear limits; sensitive information must be protected and production-specific assumptions checked.
